To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we observed the first 1s pionic state in a heavy nucleus and the second 2p state, and that we determined the s-wave part (s-wave strength and mass shift) of the pion nucleus interaction.
we have measured the binding energies and widths of deeply bound 1s(1/2) and 2p(3/2) pi(-) states, and that we have determined a positive pion mass shift of 0.5+/-0.3 MeV in 205Pbl.

(1) we have measured for the first time the binding energies and the total widths of the deeply-bound 1s and the 2p pion states in 205 Pb; and (2) we have determined the s-wave part, V(0), and the imaginary part of the s-wave interaction, ImV(0), of the pion nucleus interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of pionic states in nuclei and the determination of the pion self-energy and the s-wave part in the pion-nuclear interaction.
the study of the properties of deeply bound pionic states.
the study of pionic atoms, which are a unique probe of nuclear structure and the strong interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 1s state is a deeply bound state with a binding energy of B(1s)(205Pb) = 6 MeV and that the 2p state is a shallow state with a binding of B(2p)(205Pb)(approximate to) 5 MeV.
the 1s and the 2p pi states are deeply bound in 205Pbl and that the s-wave pion-nucleon interaction is attractive in the nuclear interior.
the s-wave part is attractive and repulsive in 205Pbl and 208Pb, respectively, and that the p-wave part of the interaction is attractive in both systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have observed deeply bound pionic states in the p-shell nuclei and determined the real and imaginary parts of the s-wave pi(-)-nucleus interaction in these systems, which is the key input in the pion condensation theory.
the s-wave part is strongly attractive and the imaginary part of the interaction is small, which leads to a large mass shift.
